newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: IMF sees Philippine trade deficit as manageable.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees Philippine trade deficit as manageable.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has said the Philippines' widening trade deficit is no cause for alarm but needs monitoring, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo told reporters on Sunday.

He said the trade deficit was one of the issues he discussed with IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus on Saturday during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) finance ministers' weekend meeting at a luxury resort hotel here.
"He did not consider it cause for undue concern, yet a cause for continuous and vigilant monitoring of the situation," de Ocampo said.
The Philippine monthly merchandise trade deficit widened to $1.45 billion in January from $816 million a year ago and $835 million in December last year.
De Ocampo said he assured the IMF that the Philippines' trade deficit was typical for an underdeveloped economy that has moved on to a more developed stage requiring more capital imports.

"Our figures seenm to indicate that most of the importations of the Philippines have not been for consumption purposes but have been for capital build-up, which we hope in a short period of time will translate themselves to export," De Ocampo added.
He said that the trade deficit in 1996, for instance, was largely due to expanding the fleet of flag carrier Philippine Airlines.
De Ocampo said Camdessus also noted that the Philippines is nearing compliance with all the requirements for an exit from IMF tutelage.
Philippine President Fidel Ramos had earlier said he is confident the country would be out of IMF supervision by June this year even if the passage of a critical tax measure is uncertain.

"The overall picture with respect to the Philippine economy was in his view quite positive and leading towards a path of the Philippines exiting from the IMF programme along the lines currently envisioned," De Ocampo said.
The IMF has been supervising a series of fiscal and structural reforms of the Philippines for more than a decade.
